title: tk cloud logs --follow and a debugging UX that does not need the Workflow API
description:
The operator-facing half of Phase 4, and it is owed from Phase 2 rather than new.

Diagnosing Phase 2's runs repeatedly required hand-written curl against Cloudflare's Workflow instance API — that is how the 10-minute step cap (2xm) and the lapsed lease (7n7) were both found, and neither was reachable from tk. Autonomous loops make this worse: nobody is watching when a cron sweep misbehaves at 3am.

Deliverable: --follow on tk cloud logs so a live run can be watched; and surface what the Workflow instance API answers — is the supervisor alive, which step is it on, did it error — through tk rather than through curl. Phase 2's rule is the design brief: a supervisor cannot report its own death, so its liveness must be observable from OUTSIDE it.

Also here because it is the same gap: worker harness output still stops streaming once the harness starts (Phase 2's 0fg shipped boot logs only), so a mid-run stall is still diagnosed from the gateway trace rather than the container's own words.

acceptance_criteria: An operator can follow a live run's logs and see whether its supervisor is alive, which step it is on and whether it errored, without touching the Cloudflare API directly; worker harness output reaches R2 during the run.
closed_reason: Completed: tk cloud supervisor answers whether a run's supervisor is alive, which step it is on and whether it errored — the questions that in Phase 2 could only be answered by hand-written curl against Cloudflare's Workflow instance API, and that is how both 2xm and 7n7 were actually found. Plus --follow on tk cloud logs. Observability now lands in wave 1 rather than last, which is the inverse of Phase 2 and the mistake its retro named.
